title: Blocked time the calendar and public booking both honour: lunch, closures, leave, dentist hours, chair out, emergency hold, turnover
problem: Hours are one open/close per weekday, a closed day gets a note but still books, `staff_schedule` is dow only, so a web booking can land at 12:15, an afternoon-only dentist shows bookable all day, Holy Week shows open to the public, and no emergency slot or turnover buffer exists — against the rule 'only availability the clinic can honour'.
change: Migration: `clinic_hours.break_from/to`; `staff_schedule.from_time/to_time`; `clinic_block` (kind closed · lunch · leave · meeting · chair_out · emergency_hold, starts/ends, dentist, chair, repeats_dow, note, created_by) under RLS; `clinic.turnover_minutes`. Settings → Hours: lunch per day, 'Closed days' (PH holidays one-press from `src/data/holidays.ts`, leave for one dentist), turnover 0–15; a person's page gets hours per day. Calendar '+ New → Block time' for schedule.edit; blocks draw hatched with words ('Lunch', 'Dr Cruz away', 'Emergency hold — same-day pain only'). `openSlots()`, public_directory slots and nextFree skip them; `findClash()` refuses with the block's sentence; desk New booking on a closed day needs 'Book anyway', the public may not.
evidence: HoursSection.astro:2–3,:41–46 closed/open/close only; 002_public_booking.sql:45–50 staff_schedule dow only; panels.ts:354–361 closedNote decorates but does not stop; schedule.ts findClash checks chair and dentist only; data.ts loads appointment rows only. Brief §1 turnover, §2 emergency slot.

verdicts.reasons:
The proposal is feasible and nothing like it exists yet. Its effort estimate is too low, though, and some of its details are wrong.

What the code confirms:
- The gap is real. No file anywhere mentions holidays, closures, blocks, lunch, turnover or an emergency hold.
- clinic_hours is one open/close pair per weekday (002_public_booking.sql:28–35).
- staff_schedule stores the weekday only (002:45–50). public_directory (014) sends dentists as a `days` array, so a dentist who only works afternoons can be booked all day.
- slotsFor() (availability.ts) skips only weekdays with no hours and slots that are taken. openSlots() (directory-db.ts:75–90) reads only public_booked_ranges (003).
- findClash() (schedule.ts) checks the chair and the dentist, nothing else.
- The desk calendar says a closed day can still be booked: panels.ts:451–454 closedNote, and board.ts:501 "A visit can still be booked on it."
- The desk's "next free" suggestion (model.ts:245 nextFree) looks at opening hours only.
- The operations brief backs the extras: an 8–12 minute turnover buffer (§ Booking) and one protected emergency slot per dentist (§ Walk-ins and emergencies).
- Nothing blocks it: RLS on a new table follows 032/037 (tenant_isolation), and the schedule.edit and settings.edit permission keys already exist.

Why "L" is too low:
- As written it bundles seven features. Lunch is modelled twice (clinic_hours.break_from/to and a clinic_block of kind lunch). Dentist hours are modelled twice as well: staff_schedule times and weekly leave blocks cover the same case.
- It misses places that also decide what is open or bookable:
  - statusFor() in ClinicPage.astro:172 and find/index.astro:243 runs on the visitor's device from the weekly hours only, so Holy Week would still say "Open now".
  - placeRequest() in api/bookings/index.ts:73 places requests for clinics that take requests, not live bookings.
  - The re-check inside the booking transaction (bookings:186–201) has an any-dentist path that counts chairs and never calls findClash.
  - loadRange() in schedule.ts:147 is the calendar's other data source, next to data.ts.
  - The Calls page's next open day (calls/index.astro:104,146) reads clinic_hours.
- It gets some names wrong:
  - It names migration 036, but 036, 037 and 038 are already applied; the next file is 039.
  - src/data/holidays.ts does not exist, and Holy Week and Eid dates are proclaimed each year, so a holiday list needs someone to refresh it with a named source.
  - public_directory does not work out slots; openSlots and public_booked_ranges do.
- Counted properly it touches about 20 files: a migration with a new public read function, public slots, request placement, the status pill, the clash rule, the booking API, the calendar's data, model, board, panels, CSS and a new Block time panel, the Hours settings, the person page and the Calls page. That is XL.
- It never says what happens to visits already booked inside a block that is added later.
verdicts.adjustedScope:
Phase 1, an honest L:

One new migration, 039_clinic_block.sql (not 036).
- A `clinic_block` table under RLS (tenant_isolation, as in 032/037) with these columns: clinic_id; kind (closed | lunch | leave | chair_out); either starts_at/ends_at for a dated block, or repeats_dow + from_min/to_min for a weekly one; dentist_id (null = the whole clinic); chair (null = every chair); note; created_by; created_at; removed_at. The app may select, insert, and update only removed_at.
- A security-definer function `public_blocked_ranges(clinic, from, to)`, next to public_booked_ranges. It returns times, the dentist's slug, the chair and the kind, and never the note or who made the block.
- Drop clinic_hours.break_from/to: lunch is a weekly block for the whole clinic.
- Drop staff_schedule.from_time/to_time: a dentist who only works afternoons gets a weekly dentist block ("Away every Mon 9–1"), added from their person page.

Honour the blocks in these places:
- Public booking: slotsFor/openSlots.
- api/bookings/index.ts: placeRequest(), plus the re-check inside the transaction. The re-check must cover the named-dentist path and the any-dentist path that counts chairs, and run under the same advisory lock.
- The desk: findClash(), refusing with the block's sentence. On api/schedule the desk may send an explicit "Book anyway"; the public may not.
- The status pill: statusFor(), plus the date-specific closures sent to the page in ClinicPage.astro and find/index.astro.
- The desk's next-free suggestion: nextFree().
- The calendar: loadRange and loadDashboard load blocks. board.ts extends closedBlocks() to draw them hatched with words, dark rules in both forms, contrast measured. A "Block time" panel for schedule.edit, with block writes taking the same advisory lock.
- The Calls page's next open day.
- Settings → Hours, under settings.edit: a list of "Closed days and time off" with add and remove.

When a block is added over visits already booked, list those visits for the desk to move or call. Never cancel them or drop their texts silently.

Defer:
- turnover_minutes. It changes every slot and nextFree, and as a clash rule it would refuse the back-to-back visits the desk books today; the owner should decide first.
- The emergency hold. It behaves differently from every other kind: it blocks the public but not the desk.
- The one-press list of Philippine holidays. The dates are proclaimed each year, so it needs a named source and someone to refresh it every year.
conflicts: The proposal names 036_clinic_block.sql, but migrations 036, 037 and 038 are already applied, and an applied migration is never edited. The new file must be 039.

Public reads go only through security-definer functions, never by opening a table. Block times must reach /find/ through a new definer function next to public_booked_ranges, and the block's note and author ('Dr Cruz away', created_by) must never be exposed. The proposal names public_directory, which does not work out slots.

One booker at a time per clinic: block writes must take the same pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(clinic_id)), and bookings must re-check blocks inside the transaction. The any-dentist path in api/bookings counts chairs and never calls findClash, so extending findClash alone leaves a race.

Every dark rule needs both forms (the device setting and a chosen theme), and contrast must be measured at 4.5:1 or better light and dark at 1440 and 390. The hatched blocks and their words on the calendar need both.
Every trust claim names its source: a Philippine holiday list must name the proclamation and the year, and it goes out of date every year.

The board currently tells the desk that a closed weekday 'can still be booked' (board.ts:501). 'Book anyway' keeps that, but changing the words and flow needs the same measured 44px targets and one teal button per screen.

verdicts.reasons:
I tried to refute this and couldn't. The problem is real in the code, and it breaks the standing rule "Only availability the clinic can honour" where patients can see it.

What the code shows:
(1) HoursSection.astro offers only Closed/Opens/Closes per weekday, and clinic_hours (002) holds one open_min/close_min per dow. There is no break and no dated exception anywhere in src (I grepped for clinic_block, holiday, lunch, closure and time_off; nothing).
(2) staff_schedule (002:45-50) is (staff_id, clinic_id, dow) only. The person page's "Days at this branch" is checkboxes. An afternoon-only associate is bookable from opening time.
(3) slotsFor (availability.ts:81-99) walks every 30 minutes from open to close. It skips only a dow with no hours, a dentist's missing dow and isTaken. openSlots (directory-db.ts:75) feeds it only public_booked_ranges, so a lunch slot at 12:00 or 12:30 is offered publicly, and Maundy Thursday and Good Friday are bookable.
(4) findClash (schedule.ts:180) checks chair and dentist appointments only.
(5) panels.ts:450-453 closedNote says outright "a closed day is allowed, but said".

Why clinics would want it: lunch closing (usually 12-1) and part-time associates who come certain days and hours are everyday in Philippine clinics. A web booking in lunch or on a holiday is a lie told to a patient, which becomes a phone call and an apology at the desk. docs/clinic-operations.md §Booking asks for an 8-12 minute turnover, and §Walk-ins asks for one protected 30-minute emergency slot per dentist per session. So the owner, the receptionist and the associate would all notice.

Standing rules: no hard conflict. Nothing touches faces, the footer, motion, the home-page chart, forms or billing. Blocks are clinic data under RLS through withClinic. They are not clinical records, so editable rows are fine. The public side already uses the definer-function pattern (public_booked_ranges).

Risks and gaps the proposal must fix. These are not refutations.
- The migration name "036_clinic_block.sql" is wrong. 036_paperless_day.sql is applied, and so are 037 and 038. The rule is additive files only, so this has to be 039.
- The public side must get the blocks through a new or extended security-definer function (like public_booked_ranges) that returns only starts, ends and dentist slug. It must never return kind notes, created_by or a leave reason. Adding blocks inside openSlots in JS alone is not possible without opening the table.
- It leaves out statusFor (availability.ts:41) and the /find/ "open now" filter. A clinic closed for Holy Week or at lunch would still show "Open now · until 5 pm". It also leaves out placeRequest in api/bookings/index.ts:73, which refuses closed weekdays but would accept a request for a closure day.
- Visits already booked inside a newly added closure or leave need a list for the desk to call, such as the Calls page. Any text sent to them must have no link and must not ask for a reply.
- A static src/data/holidays.ts cannot be the truth. Holy Week moves every year, and the Eid holidays and special non-working days are declared by proclamation, often weeks ahead. One press must add "suggested" days the owner confirms, and the file needs yearly upkeep.
- Hatched blocks on the calendar: the words must sit on a solid chip and be measured at 4.5:1 or more, light and dark, 1440 and 390. The colours must not reuse the QUEUE status classes or amber/red, and the words must say what the block is, never colour alone.
- "Book anyway" must be a quiet button, not a second teal one: one teal action per screen.
- turnover_minutes should default to 0 so current schedules and slots do not shift.
- "Any available dentist" still counts chairs, not dentists' hours (listed under Open in CLAUDE.md). Per-dentist hours make that gap more visible and are worth closing in the same pass.

Effort is a genuine L. The value is high and it fits the rules, so I did not refute it.
verdicts.adjustedScope:
Split into two shippable steps, both in a new migration 039 (never 036).

Step 1 (M-L): the truth gap.
- clinic_hours gets break_from_min and break_to_min.
- staff_schedule gets from_min and to_min, both nullable, where null means the clinic's hours.
- clinic_block under RLS: kind closed | lunch | leave | chair_out | emergency_hold; starts_at, ends_at; dentist_id and chair, both nullable; note; created_by. Writes go through withClinic, gated by can(ws,'schedule.edit') and audited.
- A new definer function public_blocked_ranges(clinic, from, to) that returns starts, ends and dentist slug only.
- slotsFor, openSlots, placeRequest (request-mode), statusFor and the /find/ open-now filter all honour breaks, blocks and dentist hours. A closure day shows "Closed today", with the reason only when the kind is closed.
- findClash returns the block's sentence ("Dr Cruz is away until 1 pm", "Lunch until 1 pm").
- The calendar gets "+ New -> Block time". Blocks draw as hatched lanes with the words on a solid chip. On a closed or blocked time the desk sees a quiet "Book anyway"; the public API refuses it.
- Adding a closure lists the visits already inside it, with a link to the Calls page to contact them. No automatic text.
- Settings -> Hours gets lunch per day and a "Closed days" list (add a date or a range). The person page gets from/to per ticked day.

Step 2 (S-M): clinic.turnover_minutes (0-15, default 0), applied in slotsFor and findClash; repeating blocks (repeats_dow) for a weekly emergency hold, which the desk can book and the public cannot; a holiday suggestions list in src/data/holidays.ts, labelled "suggested, confirm", covering the regular holidays and each year's proclaimed ones, with a note that it needs yearly upkeep.

Measure the contrast of the hatched chips light and dark at 1440/390. Re-run snap/cmp for roles without schedule.edit, so Block time is hidden for them and the server refuses it.
conflicts: Not a rule conflict, but a naming error that would break one: the proposal names src/data/migrations/036_clinic_block.sql, but 036_paperless_day.sql (and 037, 038) are already applied. Migrations are additive numbered files and applied ones are never edited, so this has to be 039.

Public reads go through security-definer functions: blocks have to reach the public slots and status through a new definer function (like public_booked_ranges) that returns times and dentist slug only. It must never return a note or a leave reason, and must not open clinic_block to public reads.
One teal button per screen: 'Book anyway' on the desk's New booking and the calendar's 'Block time' must be quiet buttons, not a second teal action.
Status colours: the QUEUE classes are the only status colours, and amber/red keep their meanings. Hatched blocks need their own neutral treatment with words, never colour alone.
Contrast measured at 4.5:1 or more against the worst pixel: words on a hatched background will fail unless they sit on a solid chip; measure light and dark at 1440 and 390.

Texts with no links and no reply asks: if a new closure leads to contacting patients already booked, any text must follow both rules. The proposal is silent here; the safer path is listing them on the Calls page.

Only availability the clinic can honour: the proposal leaves out statusFor / the /find/ 'open now' filter and request-mode placeRequest. Without them, Holy Week still shows 'Open now' and request bookings still land on closures, which leaves the rule half-met.

judgeReasons: A web booking landing at 12:15 lunch or on Holy Week breaks the standing rule 'only availability the clinic can honour' in front of patients; but it reaches into availability, the public definer functions, the calendar board and the clash rules — a genuine large.

Web bookings at 12:15, Holy Week open to the public and afternoon-only dentists bookable all day are the schedule's worst daily lies and break 'only availability the clinic can honour'; but it is L across availability, public_directory, findClash, the calendar drawing and a migration.

title: Tap a free time: slot suggestions in Book and Move, by dentist and length, across the week
problem: The time is a native `<input type=time>` the desk types; 'Next free' looks at chairs on the day on screen for 30 minutes, ignoring the dentist and the length; the Move form has no hint. Brief §1: offer two concrete slots that fill the holes ('Tuesday at 11 or Thursday at 2?').
change: Both forms add a row of the next six free starts fitting the length on the chosen day (44px chips; tap fills time and chair), from nextFree extended with dentistId, minutes and a start offset. Under it, 'Next free with Dr. Cariño: Tue 30 Sep 11:00 · Thu 2 Oct 2:00' from a new `GET /api/schedule/free?dentist=&minutes=&from=` (hours, staff_schedule, visits, blocks once p07 lands; findClash rules), each a tap setting date, time, chair, dentist. For a course step (RCT, crown, braces, denture patterns) the offset is the usual return, said in words.
evidence: BookPanel.astro:62 and VisitPanel.astro:65 `<input type="time" step="900">`; panels.ts:476–487 freeHint for Book only; model.ts:211 nextFree takes no dentist or minutes; VisitPanel.astro:60–78 Move has no hint.

verdicts.reasons:
The problem the proposal describes is real, and it can be built with data the page already has. The line numbers have drifted: nextFree is at model.ts:245, freeHint at panels.ts:589–600, and the Move time input at VisitPanel.astro:71.

- **Book panel:** it has a plain `<input type="time" step="900" data-bk-time>` (BookPanel.astro:62). Its only help is freeHint, which fills in one chair and time: "Next free half hour: Chair N at …".
- **nextFree:** it looks at chairs only. It has a fixed 30-minute length and no dentist, no minutes and no visit to exclude, so it never checks the rule findClash applies to dentists.
- **Move form:** it has no hint at all. "Place it" only picks the first chair that is clear at the time already asked for (panels.ts:375–382).

So the proposal extends something that exists rather than repeating it. That is why it is not refuted.

**Everything needed is already on the page or behind an existing call:**
- `boot.hours` (clinic_hours, via `M.hoursOf`)
- `boot.staff[].days` (staff_schedule)
- `boot.chairs`
- `ctx.dayCards(ymd)` for the range on screen
- `fetchRange`/`fetchRaw` in board.ts, which call the existing `GET /api/schedule?clinic&from&to`. That route is limited to 8 days, uses the same `gate`/`canOpen` check and RLS through `withClinic`, and returns every visit with its `chair`, `dentistId` and status, plus hours and staff days.

So a week of suggestions can be worked out in the browser without a new endpoint. There is no RLS or CSRF problem: it is a GET, and saving still goes through POST/PATCH `/api/schedule`, which takes the advisory lock and checks again with `findClash`. A stale chip therefore gets the server's one-sentence 409, never a double booking. The panels only open with `boot.canSchedule`.

**What is inflated or unsupported:**
1. **The new `/api/schedule/free` endpoint is not needed.** It would copy what the existing GET already returns. The public `openSlots()` in directory-db.ts cannot be reused for it either: it goes through `loadListing`/`public_directory`, which covers listed clinics only, and it matches dentists by slug.
2. **The "p07 blocks" dependency does not exist.** No block or time-off table is in the migrations (002–038), so it should not be part of this scope.
3. **The course-step offsets have no data behind them.** Nothing in the codebase says when a patient usually comes back for root canal, crown, braces or dentures; aftercare.ts only has aftercare hours. The proposal would be inventing clinical intervals, which a dentist would have to review, and adding it inflates the effort.

The effort is honestly S to M once trimmed, not M plus an API.
conflicts: Only availability the clinic can honour (docs/service-map rules in CLAUDE.md): suggestions must honour clinic hours, the dentist's staff_schedule days and the dentist and chair overlap rules in findClash. A chip that ignores the dentist would offer a slot the server then refuses.
Hooks are data-* attributes and must not collide: new hooks need unique names (for example data-bk-slots and data-vp-slots). data-slot-area is already used on /find/[clinic]/book.
Toggle the hidden attribute, never the hidden utility class, on the chip row and the next-free line.
Targets of at least 44px and contrast measured at 4.5:1 or better in light and dark at 1440 and 390, per the workspace's soft template.

The course-step offsets would add invented clinical guidance (return intervals) that no dentist has reviewed; the owner's pattern (aftercare sheets, bpWords) is that clinical wording is marked for a dentist's review.

verdicts.reasons:
I checked the evidence and it is accurate. BookPanel.astro:62 and VisitPanel.astro:71 are plain `<input type="time" step="900">` fields. `nextFree` (model.ts:245) looks for 30 minutes on chairs only: it takes no dentist and no length, and only works for the day loaded on screen, because `ctx.dayCards` returns null outside the loaded range (board.ts:1123). `freeHint` (panels.ts:590) exists for Book only, and the Move form has no hint. Place it only picks a free chair at the time the patient asked for.

The value holds up. At a Philippine desk most bookings happen on the phone: "Kailan po available si Doc?" Right now the receptionist switches to the dentist view and flips through days. Brief §1 in docs/clinic-operations.md asks for exactly this: "Tuesday at 11 or Thursday at 2?". The pieces mostly exist already:
- a server-side slot engine: `openSlots` in directory-db.ts plus `slotsFor` in availability.ts, which already handle dentist, minutes and days for public booking;
- `findClash` for the rules;
- the advisory-lock re-check on the server, so a suggestion never commits anything and the server still decides.

Clicking a free cell and dragging already cover same-day booking. The gain is in two places: across days for one dentist, and in Move/Place it.

It does not touch no faces, no footer, motion always on, the home-page tooth chart, texts, patient forms, BILLING_FINAL or insert-only records.

It does have fit problems, and the scope has to change:
1. **Only availability the clinic can honour.** `staff_schedule` stores weekdays only (002: staff_id, clinic_id, dow). It has no hours for a dentist, no lunch, no leave, and no blocks, and p07 has not shipped. So "Next free with Dr. Cariño: Tue 11:00" can offer a time when a part-time or visiting orthodontist is not in. The desk would then promise the patient a time the clinic cannot keep, which is worse than typing one.
2. **Course-step "usual return" offsets** (RCT, crown, braces, denture patterns) are invented clinical intervals found by matching service names. Like the aftercare words, a dentist would have to read them first. They are scope creep and would clash with what the dentist tells the patient.
3. **Soft template "very simple."** The Book panel is already long. Adding six chips and a cross-day line next to the existing "Next free half hour" line adds clutter. The chips should replace that line, not sit beside it.
4. **One teal button per screen.** The chips must be quiet. Only the chosen chip may take the teal, as "the chosen thing"; Save stays the only teal action.
5. **Brief §1's 8–12 minute turnover buffer** is left out.
6. **`nextFree` is shared** with `renderCount` (board.ts:594) and the walk-in path (panels.ts:506). New parameters must be optional, with today's defaults.
7. **The new API's guards.** It needs requireWorkspace, a `schedule.edit` check (`boot.canSchedule`), and every read through `withClinic`. It also needs its own `Cache-Control: no-store`: the middleware's no-store covers /c/ pages, not /api/.
verdicts.adjustedScope:
Phase 1, now:
- Extend `nextFree` with optional `dentistId`, `minutes` and `from` parameters, keeping the current defaults. Use it for a row of up to 4 quiet 44px chips under the time field, in both Book and Move/Place it. The chips replace the existing "Next free half hour" line.
- Each chip is a start that fits the chosen length on the chosen day, respects the chosen dentist's weekdays and HOLDS_SLOT, and leaves a turnover buffer after each visit. Tapping one fills the time and chair (and the dentist in dentist view). Only the chosen chip takes the teal.
- Add `GET /api/schedule/free` (requireWorkspace, `schedule.edit`, withClinic, no-store), reusing the `slotsFor`/`findClash` rules. It serves days outside the loaded range, and one "Next free with Dr. X" line naming at most two days.
- Show that line only for dentists whose weekday schedule is set, and word it as a suggestion. The server re-check stays the arbiter.

Deferred:
- Anything that assumes a dentist's hours within the day, lunch or leave, until p07 or per-dentist hours exist.
- Dropped entirely: the course-step "usual return" offsets. Return intervals should come from a clinic-set value that a dentist has reviewed, never be inferred from service names.
conflicts: Only availability the clinic can honour (patient side and schedule rule): staff_schedule stores weekdays only, with no hours, lunch, leave or blocks (p07 has not shipped). Cross-week 'Next free with Dr. X' suggestions can offer times a part-time or visiting dentist is not in.

Inventing clinical rules: course-step 'usual return' offsets (RCT, crown, braces, denture) found from service names are clinical intervals that need a dentist's review, like the aftercare words (and the spirit of 'do not invent PhilHealth rules').
One teal button per screen: the slot chips must be quiet; only the chosen chip may be teal, and Save stays the one teal action.
Soft template 'very simple': six chips plus a cross-day line plus the existing freeHint crowd an already long Book panel. The chips must replace the 'Next free half hour' line, not sit next to it.

RLS through withClinic, and permissions through can(ws, key): the new /api/schedule/free must use requireWorkspace, schedule.edit and withClinic, and set its own no-store (the middleware's no-store covers /c/ only).

judgeReasons: A native time input the desk types and a 'Next free' that ignores the dentist and length make every booking slower than 'Tuesday at 11 or Thursday at 2'; the free-slot API is medium and leans on p07 for blocks; 44px chips fit.

Typing a time into a native input and guessing a free slot by dentist is the slowest part of booking; nextFree already exists in model.ts and the chips are 44px, the free API is new but bounded (blocks come with p07).

Typing a time into a native input and a 'Next free' that ignores dentist and length slows every booking; extending nextFree and adding a /api/schedule/free that honours hours, staff_schedule and findClash is M and depends on p07 for blocks; 44px slot chips are 'only availability the clinic can honour' made tappable.

title: Start the booking at the slot she tapped; no Dentist step at a solo clinic; say when the slot no longer fits
problem: Tapping 9:30 on /find/ opens step 1 'What is the visit for?', then a Dentist step even at a one-dentist clinic, and only step 3 shows the slot; if the reason needs longer chair time paintSlots preselects nothing and no sentence says the slot is gone.
change: book.astro: with `?slot=` a strip at the top ('Wed 24 Sep, 9:30 am · Change') and the wizard runs Reason → Who → Confirm; the Dentist fieldset is not rendered when `dentists.length === 1` or the slot came from an any-dentist card; when no `hit` after a reason change, the strip turns amber with words and the nearest two free slots as buttons; /find/ slot links carry `&svc=` so Reason is preselected; the empty state gets a tel: button.
evidence: book.astro ends with show(0,false); paintSlots preselects from `slot` only inside step 3 and does nothing when `hit` is null; `steps` is a constant; dentists.length never checked; find/index.astro:189 writes /book/?slot=; main.dataset.phone unused.

verdicts.reasons:
Not refuted. The problem is real and the fix touches only the front end. I checked each piece of evidence:
- book.astro builds a constant 5-step list (`steps = ['Reason','Dentist','When','Who','Confirm']`, line 25) and ends with `show(0, false)` (line 407), so a `?slot=` link always opens on "What is the visit for?".
- The Dentist fieldset is always rendered. `dentists.length` is never checked.
- The `?slot=` preselect happens only inside `paintSlots()` (lines 258-262). It looks only in the painted DOM, which holds just the first `shownDays = 4` days that have slots. When `hit` is null it silently does nothing, so no sentence says the slot is gone.
- find/index.astro:189 writes `/find/<slug>/book/?slot=<iso>` with no service or symptom. Those card slots come from `openSlots(l, { limit: 3 })`: any dentist, chairs counted, 30 minutes (`need = max(30, minutes ?? 30)`). So every /find/ slot link is an any-dentist, 30-minute slot, and a longer reason can make it not fit.
- One piece of evidence is wrong: `main.dataset.phone` IS used, in the request done text at line 370. It is just not used in the empty state.

Nothing else like this exists: the only related code is the partial preselect in step 3. Data, RLS, CSRF and permissions are untouched:
- /api/availability and /api/bookings stay the same.
- The server still re-checks the slot in the transaction.
- `public_directory()` already gives `dentists` (staff with a slug and a schedule at this clinic) and `l.phone`.

The effort estimate of S is optimistic. M is more honest, because:
- The client logic is index-based: `validate(2)` and `validate(3)`, `show(2)` on a 409, and `steps.length - 1` for the last step. It needs to become named steps, with When skipped or re-inserted at runtime.
- The progress bar is a fixed 5-column grid (patient.css:231 `.pt-steps { grid-template-columns: repeat(5, …) }`, plus the glass overrides in clinic-glass.css:324-330). The step numbers (`sec-no`) are rendered on the server and would need renumbering.
- /find/ renders its cards on the server, but its filters (symptom, service) live only in the browser. So carrying the reason needs `apply()` to rewrite each card's slot hrefs.
- Every new line on the glass must be measured, as CLAUDE.md requires: 4.5:1 over the worst cover (all-black, all-white, striped), light and dark, at 1440 and 390; targets of 44px or more; keyboard and focus order.

Pitfalls the proposal misses:
- **Preselect by value is ambiguous.** Book-page symptom radios take the first offered service, which is almost always `consultation`. Several radios, plus "Not sure", share that value, so preselecting by `svc` value is ambiguous. Urgent symptoms are not on the book page at all.
- **The hit test must use `lastSlots`, not the painted DOM.** After Change picks a dentist, the tapped slot can lie beyond the first 4 painted days. The DOM test would then call a free slot "gone".
- **The strip's date must be Manila time.** Take it from the matched slot's `dayLabel` and `label`, or format the ISO in Asia/Manila, never in the device's zone.
- **A solo clinic left on "any" still counts chairs.** With the Dentist step hidden, the booking posts `dentist: ''`, so the server checks chair count only (bookings/index.ts line 196). A two-chair clinic with one dentist can then double-book that dentist. That risk already exists today, since "Any" is the default, and CLAUDE.md lists it as open. The summary would still read "Any available dentist".
- **Every /find/ slot is an any-dentist slot.** So "slot came from an any-dentist card" just means "any `?slot=` link skips Dentist". At a clinic with several dentists, a patient who wants one particular dentist can only get back to that choice through Change.

I checked the evidence in the code and most of it holds. Value survives the attempt to refute it, and the proposal breaks no standing rule outright.

Confirmed in the code:
- book.astro:25 has `const steps = ['Reason','Dentist','When','Who','Confirm']` as a constant. The progress <ol> is rendered from it on the server, and the page opens with show(0,false).
- paintSlots (245-263) preselects `?slot=` only when `hit` matches. When a longer reason (fetchSlots sends service().minutes) or a chosen dentist drops that time, nothing is selected and nothing says so. The patient finds out only from "Pick a slot." after pressing Continue.
- `dentists.length` is never checked. The Dentist fieldset always renders "Any available dentist", plus one row per dentist.
- find/index.astro:189 writes `/find/<slug>/book/?slot=` from openSlots(l,{limit:3}): any dentist, default 30 min, no service.
- One claim is wrong: main.dataset.phone IS used, in the request done-text at line 370. Only the empty state lacks a tel: action.
- A related bug the proposal misses: paintSlots re-checks the URL slot on every repaint. "Show more days", or going Back to change the reason, throws away a slot she picked herself and re-selects the URL one (or nothing).

Why it has value:
- Booking is the core patient flow. docs/service-map.md sets the yardstick "fewest steps, nothing shown that is not true, no surprise", with 3–5 taps and at most 5 steps.
- A time she tapped vanishing without a word breaks "nothing shown that is not true".
- One-dentist practices are very common in the Philippines, so a Dentist step that offers "Any" or the one dentist is a pointless tap on a phone.
- It is front-end only. /api/bookings re-checks the slot with the service minutes inside the locked transaction (openSlots at line 163, the clash checks after it). So there is no RLS, withClinic, text, billing or forms-notice exposure.

Weak points, handled in the adjusted scope below:
- Every /find/ slot is any-dentist, so "skip Dentist when the slot came from an any-dentist card" drops the Dentist step for EVERY ?slot= booking. A returning patient at a multi-dentist clinic would lose her own dentist.
- "Not rendered" at a solo clinic leaves dentist='' (any). That books on the chair-count rule, which ignores the one dentist's working days (a listed open issue). Pinning the one dentist is better.
- dentists.length===0 has the same pointless step.
- Carrying `&svc=` from /find/ needs the page script to rewrite hrefs. The /find/ slots were computed for 30 minutes, so a longer service lands straight on the amber state.
- validate() hard-codes indices (i===2, i===3) and the 409 path calls show(2), so steps must be keyed by name. Effort is S–M, not S.

The core problem holds up in the code. The bundle, though, is over-scoped, repeats data the system already holds, and cites a migration number that is already taken.

What checks out:

No UI sends either field: nothing in src/components/ws/cal/*.ts puts them in a PATCH body. PATCH has no `catalogCode`, while POST resolves one to `appointment.catalog_id`. The column is `catalog_id`, not `procedure_id` as the proposal says.
(2) `patient.notes` (schema.sql:120, NOTES_MAX 1000) is not in the Dashboard's reads: data.ts has no BASE/EXTRA column for it and no Pt field. The panel's "Notes" row (panels.ts ~l.346) is the visit's `a.notes`, read-only.
(3) finances/new.astro always starts with `discount: 'none', discountId: ''`, and invoices.ts demands the OSCA/PWD number every time.

(a) Desk notes are already shown and editable on the record: `rf-note` "Notes" in the Overview (l.791) and Edit details (intent=details → updateDetails in src/lib/import.ts, audited `patient.update`). The gap is only the Dashboard.
(b) "Nervous about dental visits" is already a question in the patient forms (patient-forms-def.ts: NERVOUS, field `nervous`). Its answer shows on the record's Overview as "Nervous about visits", and the forms queue flags "Very nervous". A second, hand-ticked flag column would duplicate it and could disagree with it.
(c) The senior/PWD ID is already stored on every statement (`invoice.discount_kind` / `discount_id_no`, migration 022). A prefill can read the patient's latest non-void statement. No new column is needed.
(d) Migration 036 is taken (036_paperless_day.sql, applied). The next free number is 039.
(e) `/api/patients.ts` is GET only. A PATCH would be a new write endpoint needing `csrfHeaderOk`, `records.edit` and an audit entry. The record's Edit details already does this job.
(f) filesLikely leaves out files that must change: src/lib/import.ts (PersonIn, readPersonForm, updateDetails and insertPatients, shared with CSV import) and src/lib/patient-forms.ts (which creates patients too), plus data.ts and model.ts (Extras/Card). The rp-warn/rp-ok pills are record.css classes; the Dashboard uses ui.ts `pill()`, so contrast has to be measured afresh.

- The reminder bodies (`sms_reminder_body` / `sms_remind48_body`, 019/036) name `a.reason` when the reminder is enqueued. A 48h reminder may already be queued, or held through quiet hours. I could not refute the core. The three problems it names are real in the code, and a Philippine front desk meets them every day.

The PATCH in src/pages/api/schedule/index.ts:279-322 accepts reason, notes and minutes but not catalogCode. POST does take catalogCode (lines 196, 237-239), and nothing in the UI sends reason or notes to PATCH. So the only way to turn a cleaning into a filling is to cancel and rebook, which gives a new public_ref and a new confirmation text.

(2) patient.notes is shown only in the record's Overview ([patient].astro:791). The calendar data (data.ts:58-60) and the Appt type (schedule.ts:24-45) carry appointment notes and allergies, not the patient's own notes.

(3) The discount on a statement is per statement (invoice.discount_kind and discount_id_no, 022). New charge always starts at discount 'none' with an empty ID (finances/new.astro:104). invoices.ts:311 then asks for the OSCA/PWD ID every time. Senior and PWD discounts (RA 9994 and RA 10754) are common at a dental desk.

I found no hard conflict with a standing rule. It adds no text with a link or a reply request, no footer, no faces, no motion switch and no home-page chart. It does not touch the closed patient forms or billing (BILLING_FINAL). The records it changes (appointment, patient) are ones the app may already update.

Problems with the details as written:

(a) A Length change on a request would place it. The PATCH treats any change to ends_at as "moved" and sets moved_at = now(). Under 018, source = 'request' and moved_at is null is what keeps a request from being confirmed. Editing a request's length would let the patient Confirm on /me/ and by text before the desk has given it a real time. It would also show a false "Moved" line in the panel.

(b) An already-queued reminder or 48-hour reminder (the reminder is written from a.reason when it is queued, 019 and 036) would still name the old service. dropStaleTexts only runs when the time changes. "No text unless the time changed" should still drop the queued texts that name the old service.

(c) There is no procedure_id on appointment. The column is catalog_id (the POST insert, and data.ts's coalesce(pc.id, …)).

(d) The migration name 036_patient_flags.sql clashes with the existing 036_paperless_day.sql. The next free number is 039.

(e) Soft conflict: the schedule's cards use the Today page's QUEUE colours as the only status colours. Amber rp-warn and teal rp-ok pills on a card blur status and patient flags. The card already puts allergies and alerts behind one small icon for this reason.

(f) Privacy fit: a standing PWD flag is disability information, which is sensitive personal information. A PWD ID number and a note that the patient is nervous about dental visits are new standing categories on the patient row. Privacy notice privacy-2026-09 names only name and mobile, the visit, and "what the clinic records about your teeth". Showing these as open pills on a desk monitor puts more on screen than the current design does. The Open list in CLAUDE.md already says the notice needs a lawyer-reviewed revision, so this adds to that gap.

(g) Redundancy. The "Nervous (+ what helps)" tick is a desk note. Senior status follows from the birth date (60 or over; it has been on file since 021). The last OSCA or PWD number is already stored on the patient's previous statement. So the flags migration isn't needed for the value it claims. A one-field PATCH /api/patients also duplicates the record's Edit details (notes textarea at [patient].astro:1260) with a new write path.

(h) It bundles three separate features into one M-sized change.

The Edit and desk-note parts are clearly worth building. The flags part is the weakest, so it is cut back below, not refuted.
